formal-choose-00.why: 'a job has at most one authorized claimant at a time, and a worker crash after claiming doesn't strand the job.'
'Model the conditional update as one database operation' tied to 'the actual claim and recovery paths', with the DB's atomicity checked by an integration test.
'temporarily remove WHERE status='queued' in the real claim path and confirm the database test catches both workers winning.'
Leaves .claude/skills/verify-job-claim/SKILL.md with one rerun command, 'the covered files/functions and sync commit'.

formal-choose-01.why: 'Two workers cannot both be authorized to process the same claim...' stated plainly.
Says to map each model action to a real code step and 'don't collapse update and commit', but never states the conditional UPDATE must be one atomic step because the database makes it atomic.
'Temporarily remove WHERE status='queued' from the real claim code and require the test to catch the regression', with a matching TLC trace.
Skill at .claude/skills/verify-job-claim/SKILL.md 'with the covered files and functions, sync commit, run command'.

formal-choose-02.why: 'For one queued job, at most one worker commits a successful claim before the job is made claimable again.'
Lists 'conditional update' as one of the mapped steps but never says it must be modeled as a single atomic step because it is atomic in the database.
'temporarily remove the predicate in the real claim code and confirm the race check catches it'.
Skill 'naming the covered files and functions, the sync commit' plus one pinned rerun command.

formal-choose-03.why: Bold one-line property: 'each job has at most one successful claimant per attempt, and ... a crashed claimant doesn't leave the job stuck'.
Says 'Map each action to the actual claim, commit, and recovery steps' but never asserts the conditional UPDATE is one atomic step justified by database atomicity.
'temporarily remove the status predicate in the real code and require the race test to fail; mirror that mutation in the model'.
Skill records 'the actual covered files and functions, sync commit, one fast rerun command'.

formal-choose-04.why: 'two workers cannot both start work from the same claim, and ... the old claim cannot authorize a later completion.'
Refers to 'the atomic update', maps it as one model action to 'the actual read, update, commit', and cross-checks its atomicity against the production DB engine.
'temporarily restore the stale-read/unconditional-write path and require a trace in which both workers start.'
Skill gives 'one fast command ... list the actual covered files and functions and their sync commit'.

formal-choose-05.why: 'only a worker whose conditional update succeeds and commits may act on the claim' stated as the property.
'Map each transition to the real claim, transaction commit or rollback...' with no statement that the conditional UPDATE is modeled as one atomic step because it is atomic in the DB.
'Temporarily remove the status='queued' predicate in the real claim code and confirm that the race test fails.'
Skill 'recording the covered files and functions, sync commit, property, bounds, assumptions, and run command'.
